skill.name: gcp-cloud-run
skill.description: Build and tune GCP Cloud Run services, Cloud Run Functions, Pub/Sub handlers, and deployment pipelines with production-focused patterns.
skill.summary: Guides Cloud Run services, functions, Pub/Sub handlers, and cold start tuning for GCP serverless workloads.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, process.env.PORT, and normal Pub/Sub base64 decoding. Manual review found no prompt injection or hidden execution, but the examples include public deployment flags, reflected input, and raw payload logging that need safer guidance.

remediation.issue: Unauthenticated deployment examples lack safety context.
remediation.suggestion: Add authenticated Cloud Run examples, describe when public access is acceptable, and require explicit user confirmation before using public ingress or unauthenticated invoker access.
Validate and escape request data before responding, or return structured text or JSON with safe content handling.

remediation.issue: Pub/Sub example logs full decoded payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Log message IDs, event metadata, and redacted fields instead of full payloads that may contain sensitive data.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Deployment Defaults
semantic_findings.description: The deployment examples enable unauthenticated access for a Cloud Run service and HTTP function without an explicit safety warning. Following these snippets can expose internal endpoints to the public internet.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exact public access flags appear in deployment snippets. The risk is contextual because some services are intended to be public.

semantic_findings.title: Reflected Request Data In HTTP Example
semantic_findings.description: The HTTP function reads a name from the query string or body and returns it directly. Reusing this pattern can reflect attacker-controlled input in a web response.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code directly places request-controlled data in the response. The exact impact depends on response headers and downstream use.

content.value_statement: Cloud Run setup requires repeatable service, function, and performance patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through deployment, events, and tuning.
actual_capabilities: Shows a Cloud Run service layout with Dockerfile, Express server, health check, and Cloud Build deployment steps.
Provides Cloud Run Functions examples for HTTP, Pub/Sub, and Cloud Storage events.
Explains cold start controls such as CPU boost, minimum instances, smaller images, and lazy initialization.
Lists Cloud Run anti-patterns for CPU-heavy work, temporary files, and background tasks.
Highlights sharp edges around memory, concurrency, CPU allocation, connection pools, and timeouts.
limitations: Examples focus on Node.js and may need changes for other runtimes.
Deployment snippets require project, region, IAM, and ingress review before use.
The skill does not provision cloud resources by itself.
It does not replace GCP documentation, pricing review, or organization policy checks.

use_cases.title: Launch a Container API
use_cases.description: Create a Cloud Run service plan with container build steps, health checks, scaling settings, and deployment notes.

use_cases.title: Build Event Functions
use_cases.description: Design Cloud Run Functions for HTTP, Pub/Sub, or Cloud Storage events with deployment and trigger guidance.

use_cases.title: Reduce Cold Starts
use_cases.description: Review startup latency and apply CPU boost, minimum instances, image optimization, and lazy loading patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Cloud Run Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gcp-cloud-run skill to outline a Node.js Cloud Run service with Dockerfile, health check, Cloud Build steps, and safe IAM defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Add an Event Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Cloud Run Function for Pub/Sub messages. Include validation, retry behavior, logging limits, and deployment notes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Cold Starts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Cloud Run service for cold starts. Recommend CPU boost, minimum instances, image changes, lazy loading, and cost tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a production Cloud Run rollout plan. Cover IAM, ingress, concurrency, timeouts, memory, observability, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: I need a public API on Cloud Run.
output: Service structure with container image requirements.
Deployment checklist covering region, memory, CPU, IAM, and unauthenticated access review.
Operational notes for health checks, scaling, and shutdown.
Event handler design with message decoding and validation steps.
Deployment guidance for triggers, region, retries, and logging.
Warnings about payload size, sensitive data, and idempotent processing.

output_examples.input: My Cloud Run service starts too slowly.
output: Cold start review covering image size, dependency loading, CPU boost, and minimum instances.
Cost and latency tradeoffs for higher memory, CPU, and warm capacity.
Follow-up checks for connection reuse and startup observability.

best_practices: Review IAM and ingress before applying any deployment command.
Set memory, CPU, concurrency, and timeout based on load tests, not defaults.
Log metadata and request IDs instead of raw payloads.
anti_patterns: Do not make services unauthenticated unless they are intended public endpoints.
Do not store large temporary files in Cloud Run memory-backed storage.
Do not perform long background work after the request lifecycle ends.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example commands that a user or agent must review before running.

faq.question: Which GCP services does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Cloud Run services, Cloud Run Functions, Cloud Build deployment, Pub/Sub events, and Cloud Storage triggers.

faq.question: Can it help with cold starts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CPU boost, minimum instances, image size, memory settings, and lazy initialization.

faq.question: Does it support non-Node.js runtimes?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Node.js. The same Cloud Run concepts can be adapted to other runtimes.

faq.question: Is public access always required?
faq.answer: No. Public access should be enabled only for public APIs or webhooks after an IAM and ingress review.

faq.question: Can it replace GCP documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use official GCP documentation for current flags, limits, pricing, and organization policy requirements.
